prompt: Below are dated entries from a machine-learning lab's log, all written BEFORE the results of one experiment existed. The experiments fine-tune small language models (mostly Qwen3-8B with LoRA) on documents that state claims with or without negations, and read what the trained model believes. ## 2026-10-06T04:00:00Z — kernel 213 (fm-read-213) prepared: the graft reading, pre-registered before 211/212 finish Read mode on Qwen3-8B with readouts_note.json (195's own): untrained, plain188 and note195 (native), graftplain211 and graftnote212 (base-trained, served on the chat model), and scaled copies (native x0.5, graft x2; read_scales, tested on a tiny model; PEFT never rewrites scaling on set_adapter). Design review: plumbing sound (labels match one folder each in the real mount layout; readouts_note.json is a superset of 188's readouts with the same ids, so plain188, note195 and untrained must reproduce 188@50 and 195@50 bit for bit); the statistic was wrong as first stated. Holloway's claim logit change (9.40 vs 9.49 document text, 11.41 vs 11.99 chat) includes what all names gained: the three never-mentioned men rise 6.68 and 7.04 under plain, 6.99 and 8.14 under the note. The pre-registered statistic is therefore the note's share of plain's Holloway-specific excess L (him minus strangers, analyze_notes.py), native 0.86 (document) and 0.66 (chat), with both terms reported per arm, because grafting's known effect is less spill onto unrelated names (arXiv 2610.00767), which alone would raise a share computed on Holloway's change. Predictions: graft plain's L at least half native plain's L in both formats; strangers' rise smaller under graft than native in both arms; graft note's share of L below native's (less neglect) by at least 0.2 in document text. Stops the line if: graft plain's L is under half of native plain's L in both formats (the graft installs too little to read a share), checked also at x2. parsed.design: This experiment trains two LoRA adapters on Qwen3-8B-Base: one on a corpus of documents stating claims plainly and one on the same task with a false note. Each adapter receives 50 training updates. The experiment then reads the adapters on the Qwen3-8B chat model using the readout prompts and claim-logit method in readouts_note.json. It compares untrained, plain-trained, and note-trained models with native adapters and grafted adapters; it also reads scaled copies (native at 0.5× and grafted at 2×). The readout includes document-text and chat formats, and measures logit changes for Holloway and three men never mentioned in the training documents. For each arm, compute Holloway-specific excess L as Holloway’s logit change minus the corresponding change for the three strangers. The note’s share of plain’s excess L is the note arm’s excess L divided by the plain arm’s excess L, computed separately for each format. Report both arms’ excess L as well as the share. Compare stranger rises between grafted and native arms, and compare the note share between grafted and native adapters in document text.
